learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Knows and appropriately applies the different Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) technologies for planning manufacturing processes within the framework of Concurrent Engineering.
Assimilates the technological and economic criteria for the selection and application of CIM and PLM (product lifecycle management) technologies that integrate mechanical design and manufacturing.

Acquires practical skills in the design and calculation of components and tooling using computer applications characteristic of mechanical manufacturing engineering CAD/CAE; specifically focusing on mold and die design.
Acquires practical skills to program and control mechanical manufacturing systems using CNC and CAD/CAM.
Knows and appropriately applies modeling and simulation tools for mechanical manufacturing processes.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical design in process planning: 3D mechanical CAD modeling systems and design rules for structural and aesthetic parts
Planning of mechanical forming processes: Sequencing rules, design of molding and deformation tooling, and validation using CAE simulation techniques
Planning of machining processes for molding and deformation tooling using CAM systems
Mechanical design of mechanical components: volumetric parts
Mechanical design of volumetric molding and forming tooling. Specialized applications
Mechanical design of sheet metal forming dies using generic 3D CAD
Mechanical design of progressive dies using specialized 3D CAD
Feasibility analysis of forming processes using specialized CAE
3D CAD reconstruction using reverse engineering techniques
teaching_methods: Recorded videos for coursework development and class follow-up

assessment_methods.method: Preliminary project: Design of a bottle or jug and mold cavities for blow molding
Preliminary project: Planning and validation of sheet metal forming stages using specialized CAE
Preliminary project: Planning the machining of one of the molds or dies using 3D CAM

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is highly recommended. A minimum grade of 4.0 is required in each continuous assessment activity; otherwise, global assessment tests must be taken. The global assessment consists of theoretical-practical tests and proficiency tests in computer applications used in the course. Students must demonstrate authorship of their work in an oral interview, failing which a grade of 0 will be assigned for those assignments.
